question: Is there flooding near 80 Pioneer Street, Brooklyn right now?

plan.rationale: The query asks about current flooding conditions at a specific street address.

claims.text: This address is mapped within FEMA flood zone AE, a Special Flood Hazard Area, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970192F, effective 2007.
Six FloodNet community sensors within 600 meters have logged nine above-curb flood events in the last three years, with a peak depth recorded of 89 mm.

Sixty NYC 311 flood-related complaints have been filed within 200 meters of this location in the last five years, with the most common descriptor being Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC).
The latest reading at The Battery, NY, shows a water level of 5.33 feet above mean lower low water (MLLW), observed at 2026-09-26 18:18.
There are three active NWS alerts at this point: Coastal Flood Warning (Severe), High Surf Advisory (Minor), and Rip Current Statement (Moderate).

Flood Resilience at NYCHA, as detailed on page 74 of the document, includes lessons learned from the Hurricane Sandy Disaster Recovery Program, specifically for sites like ASTORIA, BARUCH, BEACH 41ST STREET, CAMPOS PLAZA II, CAREY GARDENS, CONEY ISLAND (SITE 8), CONEY ISLAND HOUSES, CONEY ISLAND IB, EAST RIVER, GOWANUS, GRAVESEND, HABER, HAMMEL, ISAACS, LA GUARDIA, and LAVANBURG HOMES.

The MTA Climate Resilience Roadmap (October 2025 update) on page 11 notes that the stretch of 4 Avenue Brooklyn between Union St and 36 St in the Gowanus neighborhood is prone to chronic flooding and has been impacted by heavy rainfall at five stations.
The NYC Comptroller’s report from 2024, page 38, includes a response to a request for information on the 9/29 Flash Flood Event, referencing the MTA Ophelia After-Action Report from October 2023.
